notes.title: Alekon 1.1
notes.content:
We've released [url=https://steamcommunity.com/app/1479390/eventcomments/]a number of patches[/url] since launch, adding a variety of small features and improvements based on your feedback, and patch 1.1 is the biggest one yet!

[h2]Kickstarting Your Creativity[/h2]

Sometimes creativity requires a little push to flourish. That's why we are adding randomization to all of the customization options in the game. Don't feel like configuring every little decoration on the Celebratory Spruce? Hit the Randomize button and you'll get a fully decorated tree to further customize! The same can be done with your graffiti tag, a fiction's clothing choice, and all the other customizers.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39250894/0ed7c51636f115e88b7dd17c282065fb16bb058a.gif[/img]

We hope this change will help people engage more easily with the dozens of customization rewards unlocked throughout the game!

[h2]Acknowledging Perfection[/h2]

We were surprised to find that quite a few players went as far as taking a perfectly scored photo of every pose in the game! While there's an achievement for capturing every pose, there was no reward for [i]perfecting[/i] them all. So we went ahead an added a brand new reward for that! Highlight the spoiler below if you want to find out more!

[spoiler]Once you perfect every pose, Japley will congratulate you and let you set up a group photo at the Well of Whimsy, where you can arrange the fictions of your choice and take a commemorative photo that includes all of your fiction customizations, including colors and clothing! You can talk to Japley afterwards to arrange further group photos.[/spoiler]

If you've already perfected every photo before patch 1.1, you will be offered the reward next time you return from a trip having taken any photos.

[h2]Rhythm Game Difficulty[/h2]

One of the most common pieces of feedback we've received is that the rhythm mini-games can be very challenging to players not used to that genre, so we went back and adjusted the difficulty on all of them, and additionally, we've changed how mistakes are handled. Now, as you hit correct notes you gain points that forgive future mistakes, which will allow you to recover from early mistakes as the song goes on!

[h2]Faster Loading[/h2]

A small minority of players using older hardware have experienced very long loading times when starting and ending photo trips. To counter this, we've added support for optional texture streaming. This will drastically improve loading time on lower-end systems, at the cost of minor texture popping. This feature is enabled by default on graphics settings below Magnificent, and can be turned on or off in the settings menu.

[h2]Other Changes[/h2]

In addition to the larger changes described above, here's a list of other fixes and improvements included in this patch:
[list]
[*]Added a tutorial for mind reading.
[*]Added paper boats in the Prickly Pass river when returning after the entire river is unblocked.
[*]Added a hint about being able to switch fictions in the clothing customizer.
[*]Improved score counting clarity in Hippoli's score challenge quest.
[*]Improved grammar and readability in various dialogues.
[*]Improved some NPC cameras to better see their emotes.
[*]Increased the mistake allowance in the music rhythm games.
[*]Fixed the depth of field lens not working correctly on low graphics settings.
[*]Fixed how visibility is calculated for the Shrooma hiding pose.
[*]Fixed the Bizyburd mesh using a low detail version from too near a distance.
[*]Fixed clipping in some snowman body parts.
[/list]

[h2]25% Off Until August 2nd[/h2]

Last but not least, as part of the World Conservation Day celebration, both Alekon and the Original Soundtrack will be available at 25% off until August 2nd.

We hope you enjoy the game, and we're looking forward to hearing more of your feedback!

notes.title: Patch 1.0.8 - Jul 1, 2021
notes.content:
This patch includes the following changes:

[list]
[*]Added level names to the signposts in the level select screen.
[*]Added the ability to control overall constellation size in the constellation designer.
[*]Added a counter for the number of hops done in Wibble's jump rope minigame.
[*]Added a confirmation prompt when trying to exit the settings menu if there are unsaved changes.
[*]Added a hint about being able to edit favorited photos in the McMuney Box.
[*]Added a hint about being able to click on locked path signs for hints when selecting a level.
[*]Added a mention of holding the donut key longer to strengthen the throw in the donut toss minigame hint.
[*]Changed how Celestios' song pitch minigame can be replayed after finishing the quest. It is now started through dialogue rather than by interacting with the horn.
[*]Changed the portal from Dream's Doorstep to always activate level select, instead of returning you directly to the level when no new path or level unlocks are available.
[*]Adjusted Ray-tay's location on Dream's Doorstep slightly to make her easier to spot.
[*]Reduced the difficulty of Nekolar's crane game slightly by increasing movement and grab animation speed.
[*]Fixed an issue that caused performance hitches on Dream's Doorstep on some hardware configurations.
[*]Fixed an animation restarting in Wishling's book when the last page is clicked repeatedly.
[/list]

notes.title: Patch 1.0.7 - Jun 28, 2021
notes.content:
This patch contains the following changes:

[list]
[*]Fixed gravity taking unscheduled breaks during Yawhawk's minigame. Bad fundamental force! No donut!
[*]Fixed a spelling error.
[/list]

notes.title: Patch 1.0.6 - Jun 24, 2021
notes.content:
This patch contains the following changes:

[list]
[*]Added the ability to turn off time slow without waiting for the timer to run out.
[*]Added the ability to ask for quest hints from the initial quest acceptance dialog for Sonawing, Ray-tay, and Lord of the Sea.
[*]Expanded the pose table and quest list UIs to take up the whole height of the screen and no longer require scrolling.
[*]Changed the hover tool to be toggled by pressing the key instead of being only active while the key is held.
[*]Changed the zoom tutorial to allow proceeding without zooming all the way in.
[*]Fixed saved resolution and window size settings not applying automatically on game start. For existing players, this will take effect after the next time settings are saved.
[*]Fixed an issue that caused the rhythm game music to get out of sync if time slow was used during the countdown.
[*]Fixed the game staying in a permanent paused state if you held F1 in the pause menu then released it after exiting the menu.
[*]Fixed clothing assigned as a result of quests resetting to default when leaving and returning to Dream's Doorstep.
[*]Fixed the Snowdrop Slopes achievement not being granted if you unlock it in the demo then continue the same save after upgrading to the full game.
[*]Fixed Justaplant remaining underground after returning to Dream's Doorstep on lower graphics settings.
[*]Fixed being able to throw donuts and Albie during the interactive part of the game's ending sequence.
[*]Fixed the colored music crystals puzzle on Snowdrop Slopes not being repeatable within a single trip if solved before the Sonawings are summoned.
[*]Fixed a case where Wishling could allow you to finish her quest even if you no longer have the requested photos.
[*]Fixed being unable to slow time while crouched.
[*]Fixed the Joyous Wibble animation not playing reliably.
[*]Fixed several grammar and flow issues in dialogues.
[*]Fixed the eyepatch clipping when equipped by Dracory.
[/list]

notes.title: Patch 1.0.5 - Jun 21, 2021
notes.content:
This patch includes the following changes:

[list]
[*]Added support for using the time slow tool in rhythm games.
[*]Ensured that every pose is perfectable.
[*]Fixed some fictions not registering in photos when zoomed in very closely.
[*]Fixed Feffo race checkpoints being hard to see on low graphics settings.
[*]Fixed several spelling and grammar mistakes.
[*]Fixed photos of Oa's seasonal aspects not counting towards pose collection.
[*]Fixed the Chilling Hiraffe pose being missable.
[*]Fixed some photos not appearing as choices when selecting a photo to turn into a jigsaw.
[*]Fixed stickers not appearing in hanging paintings.
[*]Fixed the live score tool showing scores when targeting a fiction with no valid pose.
[*]Fixed the jailed Wullard lacking collision.
[*]Fixed ice statues on Snowdrop Slopes lacking collision.
[/list]

notes.title: Patch 1.0.4 - Jun 18, 2021
notes.content:
We have a bigger patch coming next week, but here's a hotfix mainly to resolve the Crockasnap minigame not registering success on lower graphical settings. Here are the changes included in this update:

[list]
[*]Added a hint about holding F1 to see all relevant help in any situation.
[*]Added the ability to start Grumbo's hard song from his dialog.
[*]Fixed the Crockasnap minigame not registering success on lower graphical settings (because some of the grass was hidden for performance reasons).
[*]Fixed the angle score for Olsy's photos being computed incorrectly.
[*]Fixed Molo's surrender pose not being perfectable.
[*]Fixed the confirmation UIs in the pause menu not being hidden when hitting Esc.
[/list]

notes.title: Patch 1.0.3 - Jun 17, 2021
notes.content:
This patch includes the following changes:

[list]
[*]Added outlines to the jigsaw puzzle pieces and switched the initial jigsaw to a brighter image.
[*]Added the ability to turn Hunter's Sense on and off after receiving it.
[*]Added exact score labels to the in-level pose list.
[*]Improved the color scheme for scoreboards to better differentiate 9/10 and 10/10 poses.
[*]Improved Orashell's swimming pose hint.
[*]Improved the donut hint to clarify that holding the key lets you throw it further.
[*]Increased the chance of Jolly Flippers doing flips.
[*]Changed the default firework type to Double Burst.
[*]Adjusted the default graphics settings to depend on the machine. Note that this applies to new players only. If you are an existing player and are experiencing performance issues, please try the auto-detect feature in the graphics settings menu!
[*]Fixed an issue that would mistakenly accept savegames from the old festival demo, which aren't compatible, and leave the game in an invalid state.
[*]Fixed the Joyous Wibble pose being missable.
[*]Fixed the Exhausted Dopey Needles pose being missable.
[*]Fixed an issue that could invalidate Qumulo poses when his illusion is in the frame.
[*]Fixed an issue that could cause the final photo taken during the ending sequence to not save.
[*]Fixed the magnet in Crockasnap's minigame being rotatable.
[*]Fixed an issue that could cause Crockasnap's minigame to not register a win.
[*]Fixed customization images (snowflake, jack-o'-lantern, etc.) losing image quality after multiple resaves.
[*]Fixed the lone wanderer Wullard having idle thoughts intended for guard Wullards.
[*]Fixed an issue that could allow the player to get stuck or fall through the world in Snowdrop Slopes.
[*]Fixed the magnet puzzle in the Glittering Caves triggering too early.
[*]Fixed Jo'keel's flip being triggerable only once per trip.
[*]Fixed cursor sparkles being offset from the cursor on ultra-widescreen resolutions.
[*]Fixed a performance issue near Bigheart's hub on Dream's Doorstep.
[*]Fixed angry Kroixes sometimes being scored as Kalm Kroix.
[*]Fixed the Winter Oa puzzle unintentionally being solvable in sunny weather.
[*]Fixed several grammar and spelling mistakes.
[/list]

Extra thanks to everyone who reported issues, gave feedback, or streamed their play session!

notes.title: Patch 1.0.2 - Jun 15, 2021
notes.content:
This second patch includes the following changes:

- Fixed a crash after the tutorial on early versions of DirectX 11 (Windows 7/8/8.1).
- Added support for vertically inverting mouse look.
- Fixed several spelling and grammar mistakes.
- Fixed an issue that would make some minigames unbeatable if you start them after hitting the photo limit.
- Fixed Beato's Woken Up pose not being scored.
- Fixed double-clicking on travelling Sonawings resulting in a permanent fade-out.
- Improved the hint text for Kuki Bird's Pecking pose.
- Made the lawnmowing minigame slightly easier by increasing the radius of the lawnmower.
- Adjusted the auto-detected graphical settings to prioritize performance slightly.

Hope you're enjoying the game! If you run into any issues, don't hesitate to let us know in the Steam discussions, on [url=https://discord.gg/V2JrR2pcBd]our discord[/url], or through email (support@alekongame.com).

notes.title: Patch 1.0.1 - Jun 13, 2021
notes.content:
Fixes:
- Fixed an issue that caused the level select menu to get into a non-interactable state.
- Fixed an issue with the snowflake designer cursor being offset when played in windowed mode.
- Fixed several typos, grammar, and pronoun mistakes.
- Fixed Ray-tay's hanging pose not being attainable at 10/10 score.
- Made the Snowdrop Slopes cave path hint slightly clearer.

Note that there was also a release day patch that changed the Wullard quest storyline to feature a much more wholesome narrative, although it is still savegame-compatible.

notes.title: Alekon Devlog
notes.content:
[h2]Intro[/h2]

The Steam Game Festival was the first time we showed [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1479390/Alekon/]Alekon[/url] to people who didn't personally know us and weren't biased to like it, so we weren't sure what reaction to expect. With nearly 4000 demo installs, and a lot of feedback on the Steam forums, on our [url=https://t.co/hHJXXhOlJb?amp=1]Discord[/url], and on [url=https://twitter.com/AlekonTheGame]Twitter[/url], we were floored by how much people seemed to enjoy the game.        
        
We were able to watch streamers and content creators play, and got to see the game through their eyes. Some even reached out to us with pages of detailed feedback! In this devlog we'll go over some concrete lessons this experience has taught us.
    
[h2]Performance[/h2]    

Releasing a demo was a bit of a last minute decision, so we hadn't prioritized optimizing the game at that point, and while our workstations had no trouble with it, some players certainly had to lower their graphics settings or suffer bad framerates.        
        
Given that we have a thorough optimization plan on the roadmap, we aren't super worried about this for the full release, but we did underestimate the issue for the demo.        
        
What's more, we also realized that resolutions above 1080p are no longer a tiny niche, and they aren't always coupled with graphics cards that can run games effectively at that native resolution. We'll be looking into better supporting high resolutions in terms of performance, UI scaling, and letting the player know that they may be better off running at lower resolutions when they are experiencing performance issues.

[h2]The Forgotten Donut[/h2]   

One of the main tools that the player gets to play with in the demo is the donut, a versatile projectile that can be used as a treat or to get a fiction's attention. However, we introduce it on Dream's Doorstep, the hub area of the game, where donut throwing is limited to a minigame.        
        
This lead players to completely forget about the donut by the time they went on their next photography trip, preventing them from progressing path unlocks or getting new poses.        
        
To solve this, we're allowing unlimited donut use on Dream's Doorstep, so it becomes a universal tool, and adding a hint for players about it on their next photography trip to the beach.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39250894/da778bb53dbec31b706740da9690fa9b466203cc.png[/img]

[h2]How to Get Back to the Level[/h2]

The first photo scoring ceremony takes place in the beach wing of Dream's Doorstep. We placed it there intentionally, so players are encouraged to interact with the fictions they unlock before going back on more photo trips. This worked well, as unlike our early alpha tests, almost every player we've seen tried a few of the minigames before going back.        
        
However, we overcorrected on this, and people had trouble figuring out how to return to the photography sections, as you have to leave the beach wing to do that. To solve this we've made Japley, the player's guide, offer to teleport the player to the level selection area.         
        
In a similar vein, a lot of players chose to start the tutorial path again immediately after returning from it, instead of choosing the newly unlocked one that allows them to progress the game. To address this, we've made newly unlocked path signs more prominent, and will have Japley warn the player that they may be wasting time if they choose the tutorial path. 

[h2]Minigame Clarity[/h2]

Probably the most frequently reported issue with the demo was that the music games were too hard. Difficulty in particular is one area where it's hard for us to detach from our biases, since we've played the game for so long, so it was great to get fresh impressions.        
        
In response, we've tweaked timing to be more accurate in the rhythm games (Grumbo, Waltok), and made the visuals a lot easier to see in the aurora minigame (Celestios). We also fixed an audio bug that could result in the melody not playing during the latter, and added restart prompts to most minigames so players can retry immediately, without having to talk to the fictions again.        

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39250894/58cc6e8c3ddcf9f4895938a3329b76c8d8d3dcb0.png[/img]

[h2]Personality Matters[/h2]

Until 2020, the fictions in Alekon behaved more like animals, never speaking or showing personality beyond their animations. Although this had its own charm, seeing the players' reaction confirmed that we took the right decision in making the fictions into characters. Grumbo's one liners alone have made him lovable and relatable to most players.        
        
Speaking of which, we had a lot of fun hearing people do voices for the fictions during their streams! We wouldn't have had that opportunity had fictions remained speechless.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39250894/da2d498388a6e7e338b257c274aae83ac9ea661b.png[/img]

[h2]Players Take Their Time[/h2] 

A concern we had while developing was that the game would be too short. As developers, we have instinctive knowledge of every nook and cranny, so it is natural for us to speedrun through it.        
        
However, seeing players go through the game at a natural pace showed us that even players who aren't going for a 100% completionist run have plenty of content to engage with. Our demo is rather large, amounting to almost a quarter of the game, but we still didn't expect players to spend more than an hour on it, yet many have passed the two hour mark without running out of content.        

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39250894/cce4c66810dbdb66da60de3686687af1cf4e4be0.png[/img]

[h2]The Festival Was Worth It[/h2]

One definite conclusion we reached was that participating in the Steam Game Festival was a worthwhile investment. We reached a huge amount of players, accumulated thousands of wishlists, and got great feedback that we could incorporate into the game. We would definitely recommend such events to other developers!

[h2]Still Seeking Feedback[/h2] 

With all that said, we are still ever-hungry for feedback. If you've played the demo ([url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1479390/Alekon/]free forever on Steam[/url]), did you experience issues we haven't mentioned here? Did you have fun? Do you have suggestions? Let us know on [url=https://t.co/hHJXXhOlJb?amp=1]Discord[/url], or on [url=https://twitter.com/AlekonTheGame]Twitter[/url], where you can also follow us for fresh showcases of game features and progress every day!
